history.dynasty: Bahmani / Adilshahi fort; Maratha-period samadhi shrine
history.summary: Fort (earlier Parali/Ashwalayangarh) built by Bahmani rulers, held by the Adilshahi, and captured by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj on 2 April 1673, who renamed it Sajjangad. At Shivaji's request Samarth Ramdas settled here permanently from 1676. He attained Mahasamadhi here on 22 January 1682 (Magha vadya 9, Shaka 1603); the samadhi temple was built by Sambhaji. Idols of Rama, Lakshmana, Sita and Hanumana brought from Thanjavur in 1681 are enshrined in the fort's Shri Ram Mandir. The fort was briefly held by the Mughals (1700) and recaptured by the Marathas; it is a major Ramdasi pilgrimage centre. name: Sajjangad Ramdas Swami Temple
town_description: Sajjangad (meaning 'fort of good people') is a hill fort at Parali village, about 16 km west of Satara city in Maharashtra, at 3,350 ft in the Western Ghats. A fortified Bahmani/Adilshahi stronghold renamed by Shivaji, it is now chiefly known as the final residence and samadhi site of the saint Samarth Ramdas, drawing pilgrims year-round.

travel.road: ~16 km from Satara city via Satara–Parali road; vehicles reach the fort gate, short climb to the temple complex

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; Ram Navami and Dasanavami draw large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Fort/temple complex generally open 5:00 am–9:00 pm (single-source; verify on arrival)
